build.//: Two Railway-specific reasons this is not the usual `npm ci`:
build.//1: npm ci deletes node_modules wholesale, but Railway mounts its build cache at /app/node_modules/.cache — an in-use mount that cannot be removed, so the delete fails with EBUSY and the build dies before it starts.
build.//2: NODE_ENV=production makes npm skip devDependencies, and the build tools (vite, typescript, tailwind) all live there. --include=dev keeps them for the build; they never reach the runtime image.
